units.label: Listening comprehension activities (A1–A2)
units.locator: CEFR 2001 ch. 4 · aural reception (section number not verified this round)
units.rationale: PCIC A1-A2 inventories list genres to be received or produced and learning procedures, but do not list this category as such; it is part of CEFR communicative language activities and is needed to run a course. PCIC Géneros marks oral genres for reception (R) but sets no listening tasks or task conditions.

units.label: Sustained spoken production: short monologues (A1–A2)
units.locator: CEFR 2001 ch. 4 · oral production (section number not verified this round)
units.rationale: PCIC A1-A2 inventories list genres to be received or produced and learning procedures, but do not list this category as such; it is part of CEFR communicative language activities and is needed to run a course. PCIC Géneros A1-A2 lists presentaciones públicas for reception only; prepared self-presentations are a standard A1–A2 production task.

units.label: Mediation: relaying simple information between languages (A1–A2)
units.locator: CEFR Companion Volume 2020 · mediation (not obtained this round)
units.rationale: PCIC A1-A2 inventories list genres to be received or produced and learning procedures, but do not list this category as such; it is part of CEFR communicative language activities and is needed to run a course. PCIC covers intercultural mediation (Habilidades y actitudes 4) but not linguistic mediation such as relaying a sign or a short message to someone who does not speak Spanish.

units.label: Cognates and false friends for English-speaking learners
units.locator: Editorial (L1-specific); no framework locator
units.rationale: PCIC inventories are written for all learners and do not address a particular first language. English-speaking learners can exploit thousands of Latin-based cognates and need warning about a small set of frequent false friends; the course is written for English speakers (instructionLang en).
